hard_gates.evidence: db-app-role-attack.txt: as erp_app with no tenant bound, 0 rows in jobs, job_attempts and schedules. Bound to A it sees only A's rows. UPDATE and DELETE of B's rows touched 0. INSERT for B was refused by RLS. SET ROLE erp_owner or erp_worker was denied, and ALTER TABLE was refused. db-worker-role-attack.txt: erp_worker is LOGIN, not superuser, no BYPASSRLS, member of nothing, owns nothing. biggest_gap.title: The job panel shows raw status and source codes ('queued', 'running', 'cancelled', 'user') in its change line and history, in English words even on the Arabic screen
biggest_gap.detail: After any change to a job (cancel, run, finish), the line under the job's title and the History tab name the changed state by its stored code, not its label. Arabic shows 'الحالة: من running إلى cancelled' and the History tab lists 'queued', 'running', 'cancelled', 'user'. English shows 'Status: from running to cancelled' in lower-case codes, while the same panel's status badge reads 'Cancelled' or 'أُلغيت'. This is the piece's main screen (see a job's state and run it again), and CLAUDE.md rule 5 asks for Arabic from the first screen. p07's record history already turns a choice code into its label from audit.choice.<schema.table>.<field>.<value>, as numbering does for its reset choices. p12 registers none for jobs.jobs.status, jobs.jobs.source, job_attempts.outcome or the schedule fields (grep audit.choice in web/src/modules/jobs/i18n: 0 entries). The fix: add those keys in English and Arabic, using the labels the jobs list already has (jobs.status.*, jobs.source.*).

other_findings: 1. Switching off or renaming a schedule that has parameters is refused to a user who holds jobs.schedules.update but not the kind's run permission. That contradicts the code's own rule ('Switching off and renaming do not' need it). Root cause, ScheduleEndpoints.Update: the request's parameters (SerializeToElement(...).ToString(), '{"steps":3}') are compared as text with the stored jsonb ('{"steps": 3}', with a space). They are never equal, so every save that sends parameters counts as changing what runs, and the schedule form always sends them. The API reproduces it (attack/schedule-update-probe.txt): on a self-check schedule with {"steps":3}, renaming with the same parameters gives 403 jobs.typeNotAllowed, switching off with the same parameters gives 403, and with no parameters sent both give 200. With {} parameters everything gives 200. It also happens in the screen: as that user, open the enabled schedule, untick On, press Ctrl+S, and the form shows 'You do not have the permission this kind of job needs.' while the schedule stays on (09-switch-off-refused-en.jpg, browser/changer-ui.txt). Switching a runaway schedule off is a safety action. The fix: compare the two JSON values by meaning, not by text.

2. The builder's comparison path does not work at bar volume, for the third judged round running (r2, r3, r5; the driver is unchanged since r3). docs/decisions/p12-jobs-compare.md says 'Enter opens the best match'. On the 100,000-job demo, typing 'Self-check of the job queue' and pressing Enter moves the focus into the list ('Background jobs: 24,623 rows') and opens nothing. The first rows for that name are also 3 waiting self-checks that cannot be run again. JobsSeeder puts the 3 waiting rows just before the last three rows, and its comment says this keeps a finished job newest. That holds only if one of the last three rows happens to be a self-check: false on the demo, and false whenever count % 4 == 0 for a small workspace. Ours still wins with a critic's path (Down past the waiting rows), but an expert following the product's own documented path fails.

3. Order-dependent test that hides finding 2: Erp.Modules.Jobs.Tests.JobsApiTests.The_best_match_for_a_kind_of_jobs_name_is_one_that_has_finished_and_so_can_be_run_again passed in both verifies, but failed 3 of 3 when the Jobs test project was run alone on the host (`dotnet test tests/Erp.Modules.Jobs.Tests`, plants/unplanted-jobs-module-run1..3.log: 'Expected: Not "queued" Actual: "queued"'). It passes only when Starting_a_job_queues_it... runs just before it and leaves a fresh finished self-check. In the host's order it runs right after Tenant_B_cannot_see_or_touch_tenant_As_jobs_and_schedules, which leaves a queued self-check due in 4 hours. Builders and fixers run exactly this targeted command under decision #41.

4. On the 100,000-job demo the seeded failed jobs show 'Tries 2 of 2' with the error text, but no tries list: the seeder writes job_attempts only for workspaces of 5,000 jobs or fewer, and alnoor has 0 attempt rows (06-failed-job-error-en.jpg). A demo-data inconsistency on the error view.

5. Starting a job and editing a schedule's parameters means typing raw JSON ('Parameters (JSON)'), and the timing is a bare five-field cron string. The cron error is clear in both languages, but there is no picker or preview beyond 'Next run'. This is acceptable for an administrator; it is not friendly for a UAE SME office user.

6. The cron schedules work live: an every-minute self-check schedule queued and finished a job at 18:55:00.9 and 18:56:00.3 in its own workspace (attack/cron-live.txt). Cancel, progress (16%, 'Step 4 of 12'), output download, rerun, filter presets, start by Alt+N and Ctrl+Enter, add a schedule by Alt+N and Ctrl+S, and the validation messages all work by keyboard in English and Arabic, right to left, with no 5xx or page errors (browser/ui.txt).
